title: LP2-49–51: directional prime paths under alternate grid layouts
question: Does the reported missing-prime set survive a 16 × 16 reshape or four fixed 8 × 8 quadrants?
summary: Reshaping the same ordered 256 cells into 16 × 16 restores all three previously missing primes; fixed 8 × 8 quadrant barriers also restore them.

scope.representation: First characters of the same 256 case-preserved two-character tokens in manuscript order, arranged as 32 × 8 or reshaped row-major as 16 × 16.
scope.procedure: Enumerate four-cell straight paths in eight directions; reject paths containing 4; keep decimal primes. Compare source 32 × 8, reshaped 16 × 16 and 16 × 16 confined to four 8 × 8 quadrants, with 3,000 global digit shuffles.
scope.parameters: No wrap or turns; leading zeroes allowed; same 49-value prime universe. Global shuffle seed 330108 preserves digit totals.
scope.exclusions: Suffix letters, five-dot geometry, alternate paths or bases, decryption, and authorial intent.

finding: The exact three-value absence is specific to the 32 × 8 layout: 16 × 16 contains all 49 possible prime values, including two directed hits each for 1033, 2213 and 3301; quadrant barriers leave those three present.
limitations: The layouts and named targets were selected after prior exploration. Global digit shuffles give descriptive reference ranges, not an authorial-intent probability or a cipher test.
next_steps: Specify a layout from independent page evidence before treating a missing value as a clue; test suffix-letter routes and artwork constraints separately.
